# Runloom Go observability SDK

Independent module for asynchronous OTLP HTTP metrics and payload-free operational logs. Consumers pin a vendored release and build without sibling directories. This SDK does not authenticate requests, access databases, instrument Temporal workflow replay or replace durable audits.

Call `Start(ctx, service, endpoint)` once per process, wrap the HTTP handler with `Wrap`, and defer `Close`. Supported services are `gateway`, `auth`, `workflows`, `management`, `worker` and `assistant` (Lumi). An empty endpoint disables collection but preserves request correlation. The supported endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:4318`, the collector within the same pod/network namespace. Endpoint and headers are explicit; never place telemetry credentials in application configuration. External export belongs to collector configuration.

Metrics include request count, duration histogram in seconds and active requests. Only HTTP method, registered route template and status code are metric dimensions. Gateway and pre-routing failures use bounded route families. Request IDs appear in access logs and response headers, never metric labels. Streaming responses remain streamed; their completion event/duration is recorded when the HTTP stream closes, while active requests includes open streams.

## HTTP request correlation (v0.2.0)

1. `Wrap` establishes `X-Runloom-Request-ID` as a nonzero 32-character lowercase hexadecimal ID and stores it in the request context. The public gateway always generates a fresh ID, replacing caller-provided values. Direct service ingress accepts one canonical ID or generates a replacement for missing, duplicate or invalid values. An ID is diagnostic metadata, not evidence of identity, authorization or audit authenticity.
2. Use `RequestID(ctx)` to read the ID. Configure internal HTTP clients with `InternalTransport(existingTransport, configuredServiceOrigin)` to propagate it. Each outgoing request is cloned; context cancellation and deadlines are preserved. The transport generates an ID when a background HTTP call has no inbound context.
3. Propagation is restricted to the exact configured scheme and host/port. Other origins, including cross-origin redirects, have the correlation header stripped. Do not install this transport globally or on LLM providers, customer APIs or other external destinations. Internal clients should retain their existing no-redirect policy.
4. Every HTTP hop records the same `request_id`. The gateway returns its own canonical ID even if a downstream response attempts to replace it. No tenant identifiers, tokens or payloads enter these IDs. There are no request-ID metric labels, tracing exporters, spans or W3C trace-context propagation.
5. Correlation follows HTTP context only. It does not persist across queued authoring jobs or Temporal workflow/activity execution. Those require an explicitly designed durable propagation contract; this module never instruments workflow replay.

Logs contain service lifecycle and HTTP completion events, with fixed attributes only. Request/response bodies, arbitrary errors, raw URLs, query strings, headers, run IDs and identity information are not collected. Existing standard-library application diagnostics remain on stdout/stderr and are not automatically forwarded. Health probes contribute metrics but do not produce per-request logs. Log queues hold at most 1,024 records; exports time out after one second without retries. Shutdown flushes for at most three seconds. Collector outages can lose telemetry; this is not an audit delivery guarantee.

Run `go test -race ./...` independently. The OTLP integration test briefly binds loopback port 4318. `scripts/vendor-observability.mjs` at the repository root is an explicit maintainer release-packaging operation, not a build dependency. It creates temporary module-proxy archives and refreshes service vendor snapshots; the SDK has not been published remotely. Change the release version before changing a previously distributed snapshot.
